name: LMH6642 / LMH6643 / LMH6644 (National/TI 130 MHz high-output-current rail-to-rail-output op-amp)
tagline: Low-power 130 MHz, ±75 mA rail-to-rail-output op-amp that FiiO and iBasso used as a headphone buffer; Head-Fi op-amp rollers call it warm and relaxed.
technology: Low-power voltage-feedback op-amp (bipolar, National LMH high-speed line). Rail-to-rail output within about 40 mV of the rails. Input common-mode range runs from 0.5 V below V- to 1 V below V+, so the input is not rail-to-rail. -3 dB bandwidth is 130 MHz (Av=+1), linear output current is ±75 mA and supply current is 2.7 mA per amplifier. Single-supply range is 2.7 V to 12.8 V, so it does not survive ±15 V rails.

part_numbers.notes: Single. The SOT-23-5 (MF) and SOIC-8 (MA) orderables are listed on the TI product page. LMH6642MF/NOPB is ACTIVE; the leaded LMH6642MF (without /NOPB) is NRND according to the datasheet's packaging addendum.

part_numbers.status: active (TI product page lists LMH6643MA/NOPB as orderable; the status of each orderable was not checked separately)
part_numbers.notes: Dual. SOIC-8 (MA) and VSSOP-8 (MM) packages. The VSSOP package is from TI product/datasheet listings. This is the part used in FiiO and iBasso headphone gear.

part_numbers.status: active (TI product page lists LMH6644MA/NOPB as orderable; the status of each orderable was not checked separately)
part_numbers.notes: Quad. SOIC-14 (MA) and TSSOP-14 (MT) packages. Any leaded variants without /NOPB are likely NRND, the same as for the LMH6642 (unconfirmed).

lineage.notes: Launched in National's LMH high-speed line. The TI copy of the datasheet gives the original date as May 2001 (rev O prints May 2004). Early National datasheet titles began '3V, Low Power, 130MHz, 75mA Rail-to-Rail Output Amplifiers'.
Datasheet reissued as TI literature SNOS966 (revisions O, P and Q seen). The current TI copy is titled 'LMH664x Low Power, 130 MHz, 75 mA Rail-to-Rail Output Amplifiers'.

key_specs.value: 0.5 V below V- to 1 V below V+

reputation.summary: Its standing comes from OEM portable gear and Head-Fi op-amp rolling, not from classic hi-fi. FiiO used it as the headphone driver or buffer in the E10K, replacing the AD8397 with a claimed improvement in transient response and drive, and forum reports place it in the X3-II, X5 and E18. It was a stock buffer in iBasso portable amps; one account says some units shipped with the THS4032 instead. In the iBasso D1/D2/D10 rolling threads, users recommended ADA4841-2 (L/R) with LMH6643 buffers and described the result as 'clean, open' with good tonal balance and soundstage. Individual users called the LMH6643 warm and relaxed. Some users rated it, with the AD8397, as 'hard to beat for buffers' into low-impedance headphones, and said it works well as a virtual-ground op-amp. Other users said it loses 'a bit of impact and boldness' as a buffer, and some preferred the LME49721 or OPA2727. All of these are subjective forum impressions.
sonic_descriptors: slightly less impact/boldness as buffer (user report)
typical_uses: headphone output driver/buffer in portable amps and DAPs (FiiO E10K, X3-II, X5, E18; iBasso D-series)
buffer inside or after a DAC I/V or gain stage at low supply voltages
caveats: Maximum supply is 12.8 V (about ±6.4 V). Do not roll it into ±15 V op-amp sockets.
At 17 nV/√Hz it is noisy compared with audio op-amps such as the NE5532 or LME49720. It suits buffer and driver duty, not low-level gain stages.
It is a 130 MHz part. Layout and decoupling matter, and capacitive loads such as long cables may need an isolation resistor.
The sound descriptions are subjective reports from Head-Fi rolling threads.

revision_history.changes: Not captured. The National title read 'LMH6642/6643/6644 3V, Low Power, 130MHz, 75mA Rail-to-Rail Output Amplifiers' (Farnell 4902.pdf).
The earliest TI-format (www.ti.com header) revision seen. The header prints 'MAY 2004 - REVISED JANUARY 2012'. The change list was not captured.
The header prints 'MAY 2001 - REVISED MARCH 2013'. The change list was not captured.

The latest revision found. The current TI copy is retitled 'LMH664x Low Power, 130 MHz, 75 mA Rail-to-Rail Output Amplifiers', which is consistent with TI's 2014-era new-format conversion. That the retitle happened at Q is unconfirmed, and the change list was not captured.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit or remarking reports specific to the LMH664x turned up. The parts are cheap and available from authorized distributors. Leaded orderables without /NOPB (for example LMH6642MF) are NRND older production with a different lead finish, not a sign of fake parts. Treat marketplace 'LMH6643' SOIC or VSSOP parts with the usual caution.
alternatives: AD8397 (the part FiiO replaced with the LMH6643 in the E10K; similar high-current rail-to-rail-output buffer role)
THS4032 (alternative stock buffer in iBasso units)
LME49721 (rail-to-rail audio op-amp that some users preferred)
OPA2727 (preferred by some users in rolling threads)
ADA4841-2 (partner L/R op-amp in the iBasso rolling combination)
open_questions: Is SNOS966Q (Sep 2014) still the latest revision, or has TI issued R or later? Searches found nothing after Q.
What does the change log in each of revisions O, P and Q say?
What were the National-era DS number and revision letters before TI's SNOS966O?
Why does rev O print an original date of May 2004 while P and Q print May 2001?

Do any generic TI fab or assembly PCNs (for example PCN20220127001, FFAB fab qualification) cover the LMH664x? None found links to these parts, and no die change or 'same part number, different silicon' event has been identified.
Which of the listed FiiO models (X3-II, X5, E18) actually used the LMH6643? That comes from forum reports and was not independently verified.

corrections: Channel counts were 0 in the draft. They are now LMH6642 = 1, LMH6643 = 2 and LMH6644 = 4.
Part statuses were 'unknown'. They are now active: LMH6642MF/NOPB is ACTIVE and the leaded LMH6642MF is NRND. The LMH6643 and LMH6644 are active according to their TI product and part-detail pages.
Added datasheet document SNOS966 with revisions O (Jan 2012), P (Mar 2013) and Q (Sep 2014), plus distributor and third-party mirrors that preserve the older revisions.

Added key specs: 130 MHz, 130 V/µs, 17 nV/√Hz, 2.7-12.8 V supply, 2.7 mA per amplifier, ±75 mA output. The draft's technology line said 'about 75 mA'; the datasheet figure is ±75 mA linear output current.
Added a supply caveat: the 12.8 V maximum makes the part unsuitable for ±15 V sockets.
